questions.q: What is the heir of a Scottish baron styled?
questions.why: A survey of Scots law of 1936 puts the two in one sentence: the heir of a peer is “Master”, the heir of a baron is “younger of”.

questions.q: The earliest Scottish letter found addressed to someone as “much honoured” is dated in which year?
questions.why: The earliest Scottish letter found with it is dated 6 January 1616, from the laird of Drumlanrig

questions.q: The Act of 1455 gave the lords of parliament a mantle of which colour?
questions.why: The Act of 1455 gave the lords of parliament one red mantle, which Lord Lyon Innes of Learney read as the barons’, great and small.

questions.q: Which Article of the Treaty of Union kept the baron’s court as his property?
questions.why: This is the Article that touched the baron: his court was a heritable jurisdiction, and the Treaty preserved it as property.

questions.q: A baron’s privilege of trial by barons was later opened to landed men generally. When did Parliament abolish it?
questions.why: Parliament abolished the peers’ privilege in 1948 and the landed man’s in 1949.
